applies_why: The judge text uses cited verses to declare a link broken, which is the action of counting a verse as an unanswered witness that the rule governs.
quote: D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.
room: Phrase: 'counts as an unanswered witness'. Two readings weighed: (1) using cited verses to declare a link broken counts; (2) only an express unanswered-witness tally counts.
why: The judge declares the challenger link broken by Matthew 1:18 and 25 without quoting the earlier-round sentence that pressed them or naming a round, so it breaches K-G4 if those verses are counted as unanswered witnesses.
